sources.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, arXiv:2001.00617v2 (2021)
sources.locator: Complete 137-page PDF; Chapter 8, Theorem 8.8 and complete proof, Theorems 8.9–8.10 and complete min–max proofs, printed pp. 76–78 (PDF pp. 79–81); Chapter 7 final early-stopping discussion, printed p. 71.
sources.disposition: Used as an independent full-lecture-notes treatment for discretization/regularization separation and the smallest-singular-value noise channel. It does not supply the local five-term proof or the finite Tikhonov sequence calculation.

contents.name: Theorem 8.8 and proof: least-squares projection noise is bounded by delta divided by the smallest retained singular value, and convergence requires a resolution/noise coupling
contents.locator: Chapter 8, Theorem 8.8, printed p. 76 (PDF p. 79), complete statement and proof.

contents.name: Theorems 8.9–8.10 and complete min–max proofs: best singular subspaces control approximation and noise
contents.reason: The B example uses an explicit diagonal finite matrix at every resolution and asserts no optimal-subspace result or source-condition rate.

contents.name: Chapter 7 discussion of early stopping for Landweber and normal-equation conjugate gradients
contents.reason: The B example proves a scalar Richardson step directly and does not import a Landweber or conjugate-gradient convergence claim.

sources.title: Per Christian Hansen, Introduction to Inverse Problems, Chapter 5: Regularization Parameter Choice
sources.locator: Complete 27-slide chapter, slides 2–6 (PDF pp. 2–6): Tikhonov convention, forward-error split, SVD error terms, and small-singular-value perturbation.
sources.disposition: Used as an independent finite-matrix treatment for truth bias versus data perturbation and the singular-value amplification convention. Hansen's penalty uses lambda_H squared; the local items state lambda as the coefficient of the squared penalty.

contents.name: Slides 2–4: regularized inverse and exact bias/data-perturbation forward-error identity
Slides 4–6: SVD bias and perturbation terms, with small singular values amplifying the perturbation

sources.title: Tristan van Leeuwen and Christoph Brune, 10 Lectures on Inverse Problems and Imaging, Chapter 3: Linear inverse problems in function spaces
sources.locator: Complete Chapter 3 page; §3.4.1, lines 354–378, regularized pseudoinverse and bias/perturbation bounds; lines 380–395, differentiation witness and spectral bias/variance.
sources.disposition: Used as an independent full lecture-notes treatment for regularized bias/noise decomposition and the need for source/noise-specific control; the local proposition supplies the operator-discretization and solve-residual terms.
